dependencies.in_flight: New authority reads and writes fail; an effect whose remote outcome is unknown remains indeterminate and must be reconciled before retry.
dependencies.operator_response: Remove traffic, preserve operation and idempotency identifiers, restore verified-TLS Postgres and exact RLS/schema posture, then reconcile pending leases, outboxes, approvals, and effects before restoring readiness.

dependencies.in_flight: Unwrap-dependent work fails after the bounded tenant-DEK cache expires; cached keys may serve only until their configured production TTL. No local-KMS downgrade is permitted.
dependencies.operator_response: Remove traffic when KMS custody readiness fails, restore authenticated Vault TLS and token/key authority, verify wrong-context denial and historical decrypt, then resume without extending the DEK-cache ceiling.

dependencies.in_flight: Model calls time out or fail; control denials, cost-authority failures, partial streams, and ambiguous charges are not converted into a permissive provider fallback.
dependencies.operator_response: Keep the pod ready-state limitation visible, alert from an external synthetic probe, stop new work when the qualified endpoint is unhealthy, and reconcile partial streams and spend reservations before retry.

dependencies.in_flight: Name resolution failure is observed as the owning dependency failing; the application does not bypass the egress allowlist with alternate destinations.
dependencies.operator_response: Use external DNS and endpoint probes, preserve the exact approved host-to-CIDR inventory, restore resolution, and retry only requests proven idempotent or reconciled.

dependencies.in_flight: The ingress owns certificate negotiation; an expired, mismatched, or unavailable certificate can make the service unreachable even while the process remains live.
dependencies.operator_response: Monitor the public certificate and endpoint externally, halt rollout on expiry or hostname drift, restore the pre-provisioned TLS Secret, and retain the prior signed deployment for rollback.

dependencies.in_flight: New OIDC login or key refresh can fail during an IdP/JWKS outage; trusted-proxy identity depends on the separately operated proxy. The app does not fall back to a shared operator token.
dependencies.operator_response: Keep existing sessions within their normal expiry policy, refuse weakened authentication, restore the selected OIDC or trusted-proxy chain, and verify revocation and exact principal/tenant attribution before reopening login.

dependencies.in_flight: Consequential work requiring a signed durable audit record is refused. Ordinary telemetry may fail soft but increments an explicit failure signal and grants no authority.
dependencies.operator_response: Remove traffic, preserve refused operation identifiers, repair private durable storage and signer custody, verify the chain, drain the authority-audit outbox, and retry with the original stable identity.

dependencies.in_flight: A missing required anchor ledger is treated as an integrity failure; excessive anchor lag removes readiness and is not rewritten away.
dependencies.operator_response: Quarantine the affected chain, verify retained public keys and prior anchors, investigate tampering or storage loss, and restore readiness only after an evidence-preserving reconciliation.

dependencies.in_flight: HTTPS delivery failure remains in the confidential durable outbox with a stable delivery identity, bounded retry/backoff, and dead-letter state; it is never reported as delivered.
dependencies.operator_response: Page on failure, backlog, or dead letters; restore the collector, drain or deliberately redrive with the same delivery identities, and retain collector ACK/reconciliation evidence.

dependencies.in_flight: Loss, read-only remount, or exhaustion of the state volume can refuse audit/checkpoint/policy writes. No local ephemeral substitute is authoritative.
dependencies.operator_response: Remove traffic, preserve the failed volume, restore capacity and filesystem integrity from the approved snapshot path, verify audit/checkpoint chains, and reconcile claimed work before retry.

dependencies.in_flight: Knowledge and vector retrieval are outside the first production profile, so a vector-store outage cannot be represented as supported-profile behavior.
dependencies.operator_response: Do not configure or enable vector retrieval in this profile; qualify a new manifest and outage contract before admitting it.

dependencies.in_flight: No object-store-backed application data plane is admitted; managed backup storage remains an external operator responsibility rather than an application failover claim.
dependencies.operator_response: Keep backup-object storage outside runtime credentials and prove it through the independent restore drill; qualify any future runtime object store separately.

dependencies.in_flight: Generated connectors, channels, webhooks, and notification egress are excluded and default-denied in the first production profile.
dependencies.operator_response: Do not configure connector authority; create a separately reviewed manifest, delivery state machine, credential-rotation plan, and outage qualification before admission.
